title: Per-route observability for embeddings + reranking pipelines
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Provide per-route observability for embeddings and reranking endpoints so product engineers can quickly diagnose quality regressions, latency regressions, and cost hotspots. This ticket scopes the telemetry, dashboards, tracing spans, and alerting needed to: 1) surface per-route latency distribution (p50/p95/p99) for embed and rerank steps, 2) show batching efficiency and KV cache hit rate, 3) attribute token/GPU cost to routes, 4) sample and surface end-to-end traces that include the API gateway, batching scheduler, worker, and GPU inferencer spans, and 5) add actionable alerts and runbooks for common failure modes.

Why now: Embeddings and reranking have become a dominant portion of RL workload and cost. Teams deploying retrieval-augmented flows need visibility across three axes: accuracy regressions (quality), tail latency and throughput (latency/scaling), and per-feature cost accounting. Existing platform metrics are coarse (global model-level) and don't allow route-level root cause.

Scope and deliverables:
- Instrumentation: add granular metrics and tracing tags for route_id, model_id, request_type (embed|rerank), batch_size, sequence_length_bucket, quantization_profile, cache_hit boolean, fallback_model boolean. Metric prefixes: redwood_embeddings_*, redwood_rerank_*.
- Metrics (Prometheus style): counters: redwood_embeddings_requests_total{route_id}, redwood_embeddings_batches_total{route_id}, redwood_rerank_requests_total{route_id}; histograms: redwood_embeddings_latency_seconds_bucket, redwood_rerank_latency_seconds_bucket (labels: route_id, model_id, stage=batch_scheduler|gpu_inferencer|postprocess); gauges: redwood_embeddings_cache_hit_ratio, redwood_rerank_inflight_batches, redwood_route_estimated_cost_per_minute.
- Derived metrics: batching_efficiency = batches / requests, avg_batch_size = tokens_in_batch / batches, qps_per_route, tokens_per_second_per_route.
- Tracing: OpenTelemetry spans with service names: api-gateway, routing-proxy, batch-scheduler, worker-infer, kv-cache, reranker-scoring. Each span must include route_id and sample_rate metadata. Add a deterministic header X-Redwood-Trace-Id for cross-system correlation.
- Dashboards (Grafana): per-route dashboard template showing: latency heatmap (per model and per sequence_length_bucket), batch size distributions, cache hit rate, model fallback counts, cost breakdown (tokens * model_cost + GPU_seconds * gpu_rate), traffic breakdown by customer tier. Link per-route dashboard from Console route settings.
- Cost attribution: emit per-request cost estimate tags and push aggregated hourly totals to BigQuery /billing/reconciled (schema tags route_id, model_id, estimated_cost_usd, timestamp). Provide sample BigQuery SQL and Console view that sums cost by route for the last 7/30 days.
- Alerting: default alerts per-route: p95_latency > 1.5x baseline (SEV2), cache_hit_ratio drops > 30% vs baseline (SEV2), batching_efficiency < 0.65 (SEV3), model_fallback_rate > 1% sustained (SEV1). Include automated slack paging to oncall with trace ids + dashboard link.
- Runbooks: create route-level runbook template with steps for high tail latency, degraded quality, and unexpected cost increase.

Non-goals: instrumenting training workloads, changing model execution kernels, or adding new billing primitives.

Implementation approach:
1) Telemetry schema PR: define metric names and labels (this ticket contains the canonical list).
2) Light-weight instrumentation in embedding/rerank proxy and batch-scheduler to emit metrics and spans. Keep sampling default for traces = 0.5% for high-volume routes, configurable per-route.
3) Aggregation pipeline: use existing metrics exporter to Prometheus + long-term rollups to BigQuery for cost accounting.
4) Grafana dashboard templating and Console integration (link per-route).
5) Alerts and runbooks + oncall training.

Success criteria:
- Per-route dashboards auto-populated for top 50 routes by volume.
- Investigations that previously took >2 hours are reduced to <30 minutes in 80% of sampled incidents.
- Console shows top 5 routes by estimated cost with drilldowns.

Back-of-envelope telemetry examples:
- Prometheus: sum(rate(redwood_embeddings_latency_seconds_bucket{route_id=~".*",le="0.1"}[5m])) by (route_id) -> p10/p50/p95 estimates.
- Cost query (BigQuery): SELECT route_id, SUM(estimated_cost_usd) FROM `billing.reconciled` WHERE timestamp > TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 7 DAY) GROUP BY route_id ORDER BY SUM(estimated_cost_usd) DESC;
- Trace example: span tree: api-gateway -> auth -> routing-proxy -> batch-scheduler -> worker-infer -> reranker-scoring -> response-serializer. Each span attaches route_id and sample_rate.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Cardinality: adding route_id to all metrics could increase cardinality. Mitigation: only tag high-cardinality metrics (histograms) with route_id for the top N routes; route_id for others aggregated as "other". Implement a route whitelist configurable by product.
- Cost accuracy: request-level estimated_cost is an approximation; reconciliation uses hourly rollups and GPU run-time sampling to correct errors.

Notes on privacy/compliance: cost and telemetry do not include customer payloads. Ensure telemetry scrubbing in worker-infer to avoid sensitive content.
updates: 2026-02-21: Design review with PM and Observability team. Agreed metric names and labels. Action: ENG to produce telemetry schema PR.

2026-02-26: Telemetry schema PR opened (github.com/redwood/runtime-telemetry/pull/218). Schema includes redwood_embeddings_* and redwood_rerank_* metrics and initial label set. Requested feedback from Observability team on cardinality controls.

2026-03-02: Spike completed for tracing header propagation across batch-scheduler -> worker. Trace id header implemented in staging proxy. Initial traces visible in Tempo. Next: hook spans into sampled console view.

2026-03-05: Implemented basic per-route Prometheus rules for top-20 routes in staging. Dashboard template created in Grafana (grafana.redwood.internal/d/embeddings-rerank-template). PM and SRE asked for cost-per-route estimate panel; adding BigQuery exporter task.

2026-03-06: Oncall runbook draft posted (confluence.redwood.internal/display/OBS/Embed+Rerank+Runbook). Set trace sample_rate default to 0.5% for high volume routes and 5% for routes marked debug=true.
Next steps: finish BigQuery cost exporter (ENG-4887), add Console link and route settings integration (ENG-4903), tune alert thresholds after 1 week of staging telemetry.
